findings.text: VMX backend exposes a helper that pushes cached virtual PDPTR values into hardware slots when the PDPTR register state is marked dirty and the vCPU currently uses PAE paging, otherwise leaving hardware untouched.

x86 core exposes a service routine that drains locally pending TLB invalidation work by checking the current-context request and the guest-context request independently and invoking the matching flush path for each one found set.

Enlightened VMCS support exposes a global read-only translation table that maps a VMCS field encoding to an offset inside the Hyper-V enlightened image plus a clean-field grouping used to track which parts need writeback.
A predicate reports whether a given CPU-based execution control bit is set in the VMCS12 image by testing the corresponding control word for that bit.

Guest DEBUGCTL reload preserves host-owned bits by comparing the hardware field against the stored host value on those bits only and writing back the guest view with host-owned positions cleared when a difference is observed.

The effective EFER value for the outer VMCS on nested exit follows a fixed precedence with hardware-loaded guest value preferred when entry controls request it, then host value when the CPU can load it directly, then an autoloaded entry when present, then a user-return saved value when present, with host value as final fallback.

After a nested exit or failure the outer vCPU model must again match outer VMCS state, which requires nested EPT teardown and MMU rebuild, restoration of the pre-entry CR3 with availability marking, PAT and EFER plus shadowed control registers applied through setters that keep side effects consistent, debug control state refreshed through its dedicated reload path, and PDPTR state refresh when EPT with PAE is active.

MSRs eagerly taken from nested entry tables are quietly fixed from nested exit tables only when the same index shows up in both tables with different values, with each such fix validated and applied through emulated write handling, aiming at discreet outer-state repair rather than exhaustive exit-table handling.

Both guest and current TLB flushes increment the vCPU flush counter, with guest flush additionally synchronizing shadow and previous roots when two-dimensional paging is off, always delegating to the vendor guest hook and discarding Hyper-V fine-grained state, while current flush delegates to the vendor current hook.
Local flush servicing checks current-context before guest-context and handles each independently, so none, one, or both flushes may run depending on which requests are pending.

Access to the enlightened VMCS pointer has two build-time forms with one returning the per-VMCS stored pointer and the other always reporting absence, reflecting whether the enlightenment feature is compiled in.

Each translation entry pairs an offset of a named field inside the enlightened image with a clean-field tag, with the whole table indexed by VMCS encoding and partitioned into guest, host, control, address-translation, bitmap and exit-information groups, where some entries need no tracking and others force full-mask reset.
Enlightened pointer load handling reports one of four outcomes in fixed order covering disabled, succeeded, virtual-machine failure, and generic error.

Guest-memory reads for entry and exit MSR tables plus validation and emulated writes during correction are all fallible, and any failure abandons normal return and raises a virtual-machine abort indicating host MSR load failure.

When nested debug controls request host debug restoration, the presence of userspace hardware-breakpoint debugging forces the debug control register to architectural fixed bits because the outer host value was not preserved across entry, while the other path restores the outer VMCS value with a correctness warning on failure.
Two 64-bit sentinel pointer values mark special enlightened VMCS states with every bit set meaning invalid and the next lower pattern meaning mapping is pending.
The enlightened VMCS version supported by this implementation is version one.
